quiz.title: Parametric Differentiation Quiz (Ex 5.6)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on derivatives in parametric form, where x and y are both given in terms of a parameter t or θ. Work out each dy/dx, pick an answer, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths Exercise 5.6 — derivatives in parametric form

questions.q: If x = at² and y = 2at, find dy/dx.
If x = cos t and y = sin t, find dy/dx.
questions.explanation: dx/dt = −sin t and dy/dt = cos t. So dy/dx = cos t / (−sin t) = −cot t.

questions.q: If x = a cosθ and y = b sinθ, find dy/dx.
questions.explanation: dx/dθ = −a sinθ and dy/dθ = b cosθ. So dy/dx = (b cosθ)/(−a sinθ) = −(b/a) cotθ.

questions.q: If x = t² and y = t³, find dy/dx.
When x = f(t) and y = g(t), the derivative dy/dx equals which of these?
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt), valid wherever dx/dt is not zero. Never forget to divide by dx/dt.

questions.q: For the cycloid x = a(θ − sinθ), y = a(1 − cosθ), find dy/dx.
questions.explanation: dx/dθ = a(1 − cosθ) and dy/dθ = a sinθ. So dy/dx = sinθ / (1 − cosθ) = cot(θ/2), using sinθ = 2 sin(θ/2)cos(θ/2) and 1 − cosθ = 2 sin²(θ/2).

questions.q: If x = at and y = a/t, find dy/dx.
questions.explanation: dx/dt = a and dy/dt = −a/t². So dy/dx = (−a/t²) / a = −1/t².

questions.q: If x = eℤʲ (that is, e to the power t) and y = e to the power −t, find dy/dx.
questions.explanation: dx/dt = e^t and dy/dt = −e^(−t). So dy/dx = −e^(−t) / e^t = −e^(−2t).

faq.q: What does Exercise 5.6 of NCERT Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: It covers derivatives in parametric form. Here x and y are each written in terms of a third variable, the parameter (usually t or θ), instead of y being a direct function of x. You differentiate both with respect to the parameter and divide.

faq.q: What is the formula for dy/dx in parametric form?
faq.a: If x = f(t) and y = g(t), then dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt), provided dx/dt is not zero. Find dy/dt and dx/dt separately, then divide the two.

faq.q: How is parametric differentiation different from implicit differentiation in Ex 5.3?
faq.a: In Exercise 5.3 x and y are tied together in one equation and you differentiate that whole relation. In Exercise 5.6 both x and y are given as separate functions of a parameter, so you differentiate each one with respect to that parameter and take the ratio.

faq.q: Do I need to eliminate the parameter before differentiating?
faq.a: No. That is the whole point of the parametric method. You keep the parameter, differentiate x and y with respect to it, and divide. Eliminating the parameter first is usually messier and often not possible.
